title: Chobanids
capsule: The Chobanids (Chupanids) were a dynasty of Mongol Suldus clan origin that rose to dominance in the Ilkhanate as powerful military commanders under Ilkhan Öljaitü and Abu Said, with Amir Chupan (d. 1327) exercising effective control over the Ilkhanate for nearly two decades. After Abu Said's death in 1335 ended the Ilkhanid main line, Hasan Kuchak (the Lesser) briefly ruled as a Chobanid strongman over Anatolia, Azerbaijan, and parts of Persia until he was overthrown by the rival Jalayirid and Muzaffarid factions; the dynasty's last effective power was extinguished around 1357–1363. The Chobanids represent one of several post-Ilkhanid successor dynasties competing for fragments of Mongol Iran.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Chobanid territorial control fluctuated rapidly over the unstable post-Ilkhanid decades; the precise extent of their authority in Azerbaijan, Anatolia, and Khorasan at any given moment is difficult to map and is reconstructed mainly from Persian chronicle sources.
